Detailed Findings
Issue #1: Create Account Screen – Font Weight Inconsistent Between Mobile App and Chrome/Web
Screen:
Create your AMORAA account (Mobile app vs. Chrome/web view)
Problem:

The same screen renders with a different font weight depending on the platform — text (headings, labels, body copy) appears bolder/thinner on mobile compared to the Chrome/web version, even though the layout and content are otherwise identical.
Impact:

Medium — inconsistent brand presentation across platforms; text that looks properly weighted on one platform may look too light or too heavy on the other, hurting visual consistency for users who switch between app and web.
Suggestion:

Standardize font-weight values (and font-family fallback stack) across both platforms — ensure the same font file/weight token is loaded and rendered consistently on mobile (native/WebView) and web/Chrome, rather than relying on platform-default font rendering.
Create your AMORAA account (Mobile app vs. Chrome/web view) (1)
Create your AMORAA account (Mobile app vs. Chrome/web view) (2)

Screen:
Login screen ("Welcome back") → "Continue with Google" button

Same recurring issue — the Google icon and "Continue with Google" text are not properly center-aligned as a unit within the button.
Impact:
Minor — cosmetic, but confirms this shared Google-button component issue is present across Login, Create Account, and now this "Welcome back" screen as well.

Fix once at the shared Google-button component level so it's corrected everywhere it appears across the app (Login, Signup/Create Account, and any other entry point).

Create Account screen → "Continue with Google" / "Sign up with Google" button

Same Google icon/text alignment issue as Issue #2 — also present on the Create Account screen.

Issue #4: Photo Manager – No Preview/Crop Step Showing How the Uploaded Photo Will Actually Appear
Screen:
Profile → Photo Manager (photo upload/reorder screen)
Problem:

When adding a photo, there's no preview/crop step showing the user how their image will actually be framed/displayed before it's saved — uploaded photos come in different aspect ratios instead of matching the app's card format.
Impact:

Medium — ties into the earlier photo-consistency issue (previous report); without a preview/crop step, users can't control how their photo will be framed, leading to awkward or cropped-looking profile photos.
Suggestion:

Add a crop/preview step during upload — similar to WhatsApp's profile photo flow — where the user can drag/zoom/reposition the image within a fixed frame before confirming, ensuring all saved photos follow the same consistent aspect ratio.
Profile → Photo Manager (photo upload/reorder screen)
Issue #5: Filters Screen – Excess Gap Between Icon and "7 Preferences Selected" Text
Screen:
Discover → Filters → "7 preferences selected" summary card
Problem:
There's noticeably too much horizontal spacing between the sparkle icon and the "7 preferences selected" heading text, making the pairing look disconnected rather than grouped together.
Impact:
Minor — cosmetic spacing issue, makes the header row look loosely composed instead of tightly/intentionally designed.
Suggestion:
Reduce the gap/padding between the icon and text so they read as a single grouped element, consistent with icon-text spacing used elsewhere in the app.
Discover → Filters → "7 preferences selected" summary card
Issue #6: Filters Screen – Same Icon Used for All Options Under Education/Profession
Screen:
Discover → Filters → Education and Profession sections
Problem:

Every individual option pill within a category uses the exact same icon repeated (e.g., a graduation cap for every Education option; a briefcase for every Profession option) instead of unique/relevant icons per option, or no per-item icon at all.
Impact:
Minor — repeated identical icons add visual clutter without adding any distinguishing value; doesn't help users scan options faster since every icon looks the same.
Suggestion:

Either remove the per-option icons entirely (since the category-level icon and heading already communicate context) and keep pills as text-only, or use distinct icons per option if icons are meant to carry meaning.
Discover → Filters → Education and Profession sections
Issue #7: Filters – Identity/Background Section – Same Icon Repeated for All Options (Community, Religion, Languages)
Screen:
Discover → Filters → "Identity and background" → Community preference / Religion / Languages sections
Problem:

Same pattern as Issue #6 — every option pill within a category repeats the identical icon (a people icon for every Community option, a globe icon for every Religion option, a language icon for every Language option) instead of being distinct or icon-free.
Impact:
Minor — adds visual repetition/clutter across an entire filter section without adding scanning value; confirms this is a broader design pattern issue, not isolated to Education/Profession.

Same fix as Issue #6 — remove repeated per-option icons and rely on the category header icon + text-only pills, applied consistently across all filter categories.

Issue #8: Discover Screen – Like/Close/Undo Card Actions Trigger Too Fast, Not Smooth
Screen:
Discover → profile card action buttons (X, Undo, Star, Heart)
Problem:
Tapping Like (heart), Close (X), or other card actions dismisses/animates the card too fast/abruptly instead of a smooth swipe-out or fade transition.
Impact:

Medium — similar to the earlier photo-swipe smoothness issue (previous batch); the core Discover interaction feels jarring rather than satisfying, which matters a lot since this is the primary engagement loop of the app.
Suggestion:

Add a smooth animated transition when a card is liked/rejected — e.g., swipe-off animation in the corresponding direction with easing, similar to Tinder-style card animations — instead of an instant cut to the next card.
Discover → profile card action buttons (X, Undo, Star, Heart)
Issue #9: AI Matches – "AI Match Filter" Slider Takes Up Permanent Screen Space, Should Be a Bottom Sheet
Screen:
AI Matches → "AI Match Filter" (compatibility % slider) section
Problem:
The AI Match Filter slider is permanently embedded inline at the top of the AI Matches screen, taking up significant vertical space before users even see any recommendations.
Impact:

Medium — pushes actual match content further down the screen, adds visual clutter, and doesn't follow the pattern used elsewhere in the app (e.g., regular Filters) where refinement controls are tucked away until needed.
Suggestion:

Move this into a collapsed "Match Filter" button/chip that, when tapped, opens the slider in a bottom sheet/modal (sliding up from the bottom) — similar to how Discover's Filters work — so the main AI Matches screen stays clean and recommendation-focused by default.

Issue #10: Safety Center – "Verified Profile" and "Face Verification" Redirect to the Same Screen
Screen:
Safety Center → Verification section ("Verified Profile", "Photo Verification", "Face Verification")
Problem:
Tapping "Verified Profile" and tapping "Face Verification" both lead to the same screen — making one of them redundant.
Impact:
Medium — confusing UX, since users would expect each distinct menu item to lead to its own distinct flow (identity verification status vs. actual selfie/face verification flow).
Suggestion:

Either differentiate the destinations properly (e.g., "Verified Profile" shows overall verification status/summary, while "Face Verification" launches the actual selfie verification flow), or remove one of the two entries if they're genuinely meant to be the same action.
Safety Center → Verification section ("Verified Profile", "Photo Verification", "Face Verification")
Issue #11: Settings – "Membership" and "Manage Subscription" Redirect to the Same Screen
Screen:
Settings → Membership section ("Membership", "Manage Subscription")
Problem:
Same recurring pattern as earlier duplicate-link issues — "Membership" and "Manage Subscription" both lead to the same screen instead of distinct destinations.
Impact:

Medium — confirms this duplicate-link pattern is recurring across multiple sections of the app (legal links, safety/verification, and now membership), suggesting a systemic issue with how menu items are wired up.
Suggestion:

Differentiate the two — "Membership" should show plan options/benefits (browse/upgrade), while "Manage Subscription" should show the user's current plan, billing details, and cancellation options. Audit the rest of the app for similar duplicate-destination links.
Settings → Membership section ("Membership", "Manage Subscription")
Issue #12: Verification Flow – Connector Lines Between Steps Look Broken/Unpolished
Screen:
Verification flow (Aadhaar → Selfie → Processing → Verified) — step progress indicator
Problem:

The vertical connector lines between each verification step appear as short, disconnected dashes rather than a continuous, properly styled progress line — looks unfinished/glitchy rather than an intentional stepper UI.
Impact:
Minor-Medium — this is a multi-step verification flow (identity-related, so trust matters here); a broken-looking progress indicator can undermine user confidence in an already sensitive process.
Suggestion:

Redesign the connector as a continuous vertical line (or properly spaced dashed line if intended) that visually connects each step icon, with a clear filled/unfilled state to show progress — similar to standard stepper/timeline UI patterns.
Verification flow (Aadhaar → Selfie → Processing → Verified) — step progress indicator
Issue #13: Profile Screen – "My dating identity" Title Doesn't Look Polished / Not in Proper Case
Screen:
Profile → header title ("My dating identity")
Problem:

The screen title "My dating identity" is written in sentence case rather than a consistent, polished title case (e.g., "My Dating Identity"), and doesn't feel visually strong as a section header compared to other screen titles in the app.
Impact:
Minor — cosmetic/consistency issue, but title casing should follow a consistent standard across the app (other headers like "Photo Manager", "Safety Center", "AI Matches" all use Title Case).
Suggestion:
Update to Title Case ("My Dating Identity") to match the casing convention used across the rest of the app's screen titles, and review other headers for the same consistency.
Profile → header title ("My dating identity")
Issue #14: Profile – Same Sub-sections (Photos, Prompts, Interests, etc.) Duplicated Across Profile, Edit Profile, and Complete Your Profile Screens
Screen:
Profile → Edit Profile → Complete Your Profile (all three)
Problem:

The same management options — Manage Photos, Profile Prompts, Interests, and other profile sections — appear repeated across three separate screens (main Profile, Edit Profile, and Complete Your Profile) instead of living in one place.
Impact:

High — creates a confusing, overlapping information architecture; users don't know which screen is the "correct" place to manage a given section, and maintaining the same options in three places increases risk of inconsistent states and duplicated logic.
Suggestion:

Consolidate into a single source of truth for profile editing. Keep "Complete Your Profile" purely as a progress/completion dashboard that deep-links into specific sections, and keep "Edit Profile" as the one actual editing screen.
Issue #15: App-Wide – Font Weight & Size Inconsistent Between Chrome/Web and Mobile
Screen:
App-wide (all screens) — Chrome/web view vs. mobile app view
Problem:

Same systemic issue as Issue #1, now confirmed to be app-wide rather than limited to the Create Account screen — font weight and size render differently between the Chrome/web version and the mobile app version across the entire app, not just one screen.
Impact:
High — this isn't a one-off cosmetic bug but a foundational design-system/typography issue affecting brand consistency and readability across the entire product on every screen.
Suggestion:

Audit and standardize the typography system app-wide — define a single shared type scale (font family, weights, sizes, line-heights) as design tokens, and ensure both the mobile app and web/Chrome build consume the exact same values instead of relying on platform-default rendering.

Issue #18: Global – Screen Title Font Size & Weight Inconsistent Across Chats, AI Matches, Events, and Profile
Screen:
Chats ("Chats"), AI Matches ("AI Matches"), Events ("Events"), Profile ("My dating identity") — all top-level screen titles
Problem:

The main screen title text (top-left header on each tab) varies in font size and weight across the four screens — some titles appear bolder/larger, others noticeably smaller/lighter, with no consistent type scale applied to what should be an identical "page title" style component.
Impact:

Medium — reinforces the broader typography inconsistency already flagged (Issues #1, #13, #15); top-level navigation titles are a core, highly visible brand element, so inconsistency here is especially noticeable to users moving between tabs.
Suggestion:

Define one fixed "Screen Title" text style (exact font size, weight, and color) as a shared component/token, and apply it identically to every tab's header — Discover, Chats, AI Matches, Events, Profile — instead of styling each screen's title independently.
